newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwan's Chang begins damage control in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Chang begins damage control in S.Africa.

text.p: Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang arrived in Johannesburg on Tuesday for talks on bilateral links after South Africa's decision to switch diplomatic relations from Taiwan to China.

He was greeted at Johannesburg International Airport by a crowd of around 200 Taiwanese nationals living in South Africa. Chang spoke briefly to reporters, saying only he hoped to meet President Nelson Mandela during his stay.

Chang was scheduled to begin a round of diplomatic talks on Tuesday in an effort to secure the highest possible relations with South Africa after its announcement on November 27 that Pretoria would sever links with Taipei from 1997 to favour Beijing.
The South African president's office said Mandela had arranged to meet Chang on Wednesday.
"A meeting will take place at about 12 'o clock (1000 GMT) tomorrow in Pretoria," Mandela's spokesman, Parks Mankahlana, told Reuters. He did not elaborate.

South Africa is the biggest of only 30 countries -- mostly underdeveloped states in central America and Africa -- that recognise Taiwan's Republic of China government rather than the communist People's Republic of China on the mainland.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to international ties since the two split after a civil war in 1949.
